content.value_statement: React failures often hide behind silent returns and weak error messages. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for logs, tracing, and safer diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to replace silent early returns with contextual warning logs.
Shows how to write diagnostic error messages with function, state, and likely cause details.
Defines structured logging levels and a small logger wrapper for React code.
Demonstrates redaction of sensitive keys before logging application context.
Covers flow tracing, state snapshots, assertion helpers, Sentry reporting, and React error boundaries.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not install a logging library or monitoring backend.
Examples need adaptation for each project logging policy and privacy rules.
It does not provide dashboards, alert rules, or distributed tracing infrastructure.
It cannot verify production telemetry quality without access to real logs and incidents.

use_cases.title: Add Debuggable React Flows
use_cases.description: Use the skill to add clear logs around async flows, state changes, and early returns.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Incident Context
use_cases.description: Use the patterns to capture useful error details while avoiding sensitive data in reports.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Logging Practices
use_cases.description: Use the checklist and examples to align React and React Native contributors on observable code.

prompt_templates.title: Review Logging Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one component or hook.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-observability skill to review this React code. Identify silent returns, weak error messages, and missing context logs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Structured Logs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation task for a feature flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-observability skill to add structured logging to this React flow. Include log levels, context objects, and sensitive-data redaction guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-observability skill to design error handling for this feature. Include assertion helpers, error boundaries, and production reporting points.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Incident Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-observability skill to analyze this production incident path. Recommend logs, state snapshots, flow identifiers, and redaction rules.

output_examples.input: A React checkout flow fails without useful logs.
output: A list of silent branches that need warning or error logs.
Recommended flow identifiers for checkout steps and failure points.
Sensitive fields that should be redacted before logging or reporting.

output_examples.input: A component catches errors but only shows a generic message.
output: A clearer diagnostic message structure for developers.
User-safe fallback guidance for the visible interface.
Suggested production error reporting context without secrets.

output_examples.input: A team wants a shared React logging convention.
output: Recommended logging levels and when to use each level.
A checklist for early returns, state snapshots, and error boundaries.
Anti-patterns to avoid before merging new instrumentation.

best_practices: Log why code exits early, and include only the context needed to diagnose the branch.
Redact sensitive fields before sending context to consoles or error reporting services.
Use consistent flow identifiers so one user action can be traced across multiple steps.
anti_patterns: Do not add broad state dumps to production logs without privacy review.
Do not swallow caught errors after logging unless the behavior is intentional and documented.
Do not leave temporary debug logging enabled without a flag or clear removal plan.

faq.question: Does this skill work with React Native?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to React web and React Native, but platform logging tools may differ.

faq.question: Does it install Sentry or another service?
faq.answer: No. It shows integration patterns, but dependency choice and setup remain project decisions.

faq.question: Can it prevent sensitive data from being logged?
faq.answer: It provides redaction patterns and review prompts. Teams still need project-specific privacy rules.

faq.question: Is this only for production incidents?
faq.answer: No. It also helps during feature development, debugging, and code review.

faq.question: What files should I provide when using it?
faq.answer: Provide the component, hook, flow code, logger utilities, and any error boundary or reporting code.

faq.question: Can it replace observability infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It improves application instrumentation patterns, but it does not provide storage, dashboards, or alerts.
